en: The Sutra on the Dhāraṇī of Knowledge of Past Lives Spoken by the Buddha,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Imperial Censor, Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments,
Great Master of Enlightened Teaching, Subject Faxian, by Imperial Decree.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Ānanda, saying:
"There is a dhāraṇī named 'Knowledge of Past Lives.
If there are sentient beings who hear this dhāraṇī,"
Those who are able to receive and uphold this with a sincere heart will have all their most grievous karmic offenses from throughout a thousand kalpas completely extinguished.
If one can maintain this without interruption for the duration of one's life, [the merit shall be even greater].
This person shall constantly know their past lives throughout seventy million births.
*Namo ratnaśikhiṇe tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya | Tadyathā | Oṃ ratne ratne surate ratnapraveśe mahāratnakiṇi ratnasambhave svāhā.* At that time, Ānanda heard the Buddha’s proclamation.
Having enabled all sentient beings to attain the dhāraṇī of the knowledge of past lives,
they marveled at this unprecedented occurrence and rejoiced immeasurably;
they then prostrated with their heads at the Buddha's feet and withdrew.
